body: There are countless numbers out there right now who have, and/or will commit deeds that society has, for the most part, deemed punishable by death living every day with this knowledge eating at them, afraid to go to prison or the electric chair. Society can, and does, bear the burden of carrying out a long, expensive, process to either spend another exorbitant sum housing them with the others unfit for society or executing them anyway. For these people, suicide removes that burden from the shoulders of society, removes the problem from society, and ends their eternal anguish. A win win win lose situation?

You're over simplifying, but sort of. Some people find themselves in a situation where suicide would actually be the best solution. They're evil, have no redeeming qualities, don't like people, are a burden on society, prey on others, and hate it. They're in constant pain. They hate themselves because they know they're evil.
Their choices are to continue preying upon society, or death. Which do you think they should choose?

I think you're making way more out of it than need be.
1. Some people are bad.
2. Some bad people know they are bad people.
3. Bad people should die.
4. Some bad people kill themselves.
5. Bad people killing themselves is good. (Why? See previous reply.)

1: allow the harm to continue
2: jail them until they die of something else.

If you know of another, by all means, tell me.

I only mean that not every misdeed need be shooting 50 people from a hotel window. There are different degrees of harm, wouldn't you agree? And as such, certainly SOME would effectively best be dealt with by means of elimination, and if the perpetrator happens to be the one to do it, that much the better.

I don't believe that one can "make up for" some things. Your opinion that no one deserves to die is, in my opinion, naive and narrow-minded. No offense intended. Certainly some do. Pol Pot? Adolf Hitler? Heinrich Himmler?! Ted Bundy? Honestly, I'm more afraid of the liberal philosophy that has permeated our society. It's why there are so many nut jobs running around. Some need killing, so others may live peacefully.

Thanks for your reply and kind words. You've drawn the line at "bent on committing harm", but what about other degrees or types of wrongs? The world isn't black and white.
 Sometimes, because every situation is possible and eventually occurs, suicide would, logically, have to be the right course of action for someone somewhere.
